title: HfO2-MgF2 Fabry-Perot Cavity Bandpass Filter for Solar-Blind UV
scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity design with HfO2/MgF2 distributed Bragg reflectors can achieve high transmittance in 255-280 nm while suppressing 300-1100 nm, with performance improving as cavity thickness is tuned.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Bandpass filters use high/low index pairs to create reflector stacks, with a cavity layer between them creating a transmission peak at the design wavelength. Quarter-wave optical thickness at center wavelength creates constructive interference in the passband. MgF2 has low UV absorption; HfO2 provides sufficient index contrast.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | SiO2 substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers (nm)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
Keep total layer count at exactly 29 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30 limit)
All materials are conventional depositable inorganic dielectrics
Layer thicknesses should remain in practical deposition range (20-200 nm typical)
theory_basis: Recalled: Fabry-Perot cavity filters use two reflector stacks separated by a spacer layer to create a transmission band
Recalled: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) at center wavelength maximizes reflector performance
Recalled: MgF2 has good transmission down to ~120 nm UV range
Recalled: HfO2 provides index contrast ~2.0-2.1 in UV versus MgF2 ~1.4
Recalled: More reflector pairs increase bandwidth selectivity but add layers
Recalled: Symmetric cavity designs reduce sidelobes in the stopband
expected_advantages: HfO2/MgF2 pair is commonly used for UV coatings from recalled knowledge
29 layers provides sufficient reflector pairs for good blocking
Cavity design naturally creates the required bandpass behavior
All materials are in the guaranteed resolution list
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 has acceptable absorption at 255-280 nm - would need to check extinction coefficient data
Uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal versus fewer layers with different topology - this is a recalled rule of thumb
Uncertain about the exact index values at UV wavelengths - using recalled approximate values
Angle of incidence not specified in request - assuming normal incidence, but space platform may have off-axis rays
Polarization effects not addressed - may matter for oblique incidence in orbit
Would need to verify MgF2 stress properties for space environment qualification
execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar multilayer filter coating on fused silica (SiO2 (Gao)) substrate with air incidence. Use only hfo2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) as coating materials in the following fixed sequence from air side: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2. Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses as independent variables. Target: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm wavelength band, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm band, minimize transmittance in 700-1100 nm band. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Total layer count fixed at 29.
